solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flog a riverboat, partially capsized in Amazon?

indicators.note: capsized says the hidden letters are read backwards
partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone beating a riverboat that has half overturned somewhere on the Amazon river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon' looks like the river, but it is a warrior woman. 'Partially' picks OGARIV from 'Flog a riverboat' and 'capsized' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are words for a fierce, domineering woman; the Amazons were legendary female warriors.

clue.text: Maybe Pete for instance chases Penny, and Lira later

indicators.note: chases means comes after, so the abbreviation follows the penny's letter
later says the same 'for instance' abbreviation comes again, this time after the lira's letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for the Italian lira

explanation.surface: Someone called Pete follows a penny, then a lira, as if chasing loose change.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'for instance' abbreviation EG is used twice: once after P (Penny) and again, 'later', after L (Lira).
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Pete, the Disney cat villain, is known as Peg-Leg Pete for his wooden limb.

clue.text: Ship's service in Arctic rarer, I worked out

indicators.note: in says the service's letters sit inside the rearranged letters
worked out suggests a problem solved, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A naval vessel whose service in rare Arctic conditions has been figured out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' reads as the ship's duty, but it is an armed service, the Royal Air Force. 'worked out' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft carrier is a large warship with a flight deck, a kind of naval vessel.

clue.text: Irony of flying officer hiding mistake over America

indicators.note: over places this group above the next in a down answer
hiding means the officer's letters enclose the mistake

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for a Flying Officer in the RAF
to err is to make a mistake; ERR stands for it here
US is America

explanation.surface: Irony seen in an air force officer covering up an error affecting America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irony' reads as sarcasm but means 'of iron'. In a down clue 'over' puts FERR on top of US.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrous is the chemistry adjective for containing iron, which is what 'irony' literally means here.

clue.text: As I put onion tart out: 'That's the limit!'

indicators.note: out suggests the words are put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook exasperated at having to throw out an onion tart: enough is enough!
explanation.definitionFit: Saturation point is the stage beyond which nothing more can be absorbed or tolerated: the limit.

clue.text: Plantsman Brown features in various obits

indicators.note: features in says the colour appears within the other letters
various suggests different arrangements, so the letters of obits are mixed

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A gardener named Brown gets mentioned in several obituaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname but is a colour. 'various' rearranges the obits letters into BOIST, which 'features in' then opens to take the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanist is a scientist who studies plants, so a plantsman in the expert sense.

clue.text: Bearing sleeve needed for jet

parts.note: air can mean bearing or manner, as in an air of confidence
a liner is a protective sleeve, as for a cylinder or record

explanation.surface: An engineering part: a bearing sleeve is required for a jet engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing sleeve' reads as one machine part, but 'Bearing' is a person's manner, AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet is a passenger aircraft; an airliner is a large plane carrying passengers.

clue.text: Without admitting it, food store's a diversion

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: sine is Latin for without, as in sine qua non
a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared food

explanation.surface: A food shop running a little side business without owning up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points forward to the food store: 'Without' (Latin SINE) is 'admitting' DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideline is an activity pursued alongside one's main work, a secondary diversion.

clue.text: American fellow's a handsome chap

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
the 's in fellow's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Saying that an American man is good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of fellow's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so his name is used for any good-looking young man.

clue.text: Groovy time of excitement?

definitions.meaning: playfully read as 'like a groove': a long track worn into the ground
the annual mating season of deer, when stags are aroused

explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' is 1960s slang for great, but here it means 'of grooves'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut is both a worn track in the ground and the deer breeding season.

clue.text: Transport for Secretary of State for Transport suspended!

parts.note: Vince Cable was the Business Secretary in the coalition government of the time
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Headline: the Transport Secretary has been suspended from office!
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended!' fits the whole: the cars hang from a cable. Vince Cable was a UK cabinet minister, Business Secretary, when the puzzle ran.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable car is a passenger carriage hauled along an overhead wire, a form of transport.

clue.text: Lacking part of machine-gun, a Blenheim is powerless

indicators.note: lacking part of tells you to drop the surplus letters at each end, leaving a run inside

explanation.surface: A wartime Blenheim bomber with a broken machine-gun is defenceless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blenheim was a British WWII bomber. 'Lacking part of' strips the outer letters to leave UNABLE inside 'machine-gun, a Blenheim'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable means lacking the power or capacity to do something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Onion glut a cart's transporting produces 'bouquet'

indicators.note: transporting can mean carrying away in rapture, so the letters are sent into a new order

explanation.surface: A cart laden with a glut of onions makes a tribute of a sort.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of cart's is part of the fodder. 'transporting' signals the anagram; 'produces' is a link. A bouquet is a compliment, not just flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet can be figurative praise, like a tribute paid; congratulations are such praise.

clue.text: Unguent regularly given to pigeon

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Ointment is routinely applied to a sick pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: The nun is a breed of fancy domestic pigeon with a hood-like crest.

clue.text: With odds and ends in tin, amateur finds choral work

parts.note: a can is a tin
tat is cheap junk, odds and ends

explanation.surface: An amateur singer with a tin of bits and pieces manages to perform a choral piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is CAN + TAT + A; 'With' and 'in' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a musical composition for voices, often a chorus and soloists.

clue.text: Game with Gillingham initially in a state — defence …

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the others

parts.note: IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa, a US state
polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: Gillingham's football game left their fans in a state, and the defence is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Gillingham is an English football club. 'in' puts POLOG between A and IA.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence of one's opinions or conduct.

clue.text: … having problem with pitch — possible defeat on

indicators.note: possible means a possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Continuing 16: a defence with trouble on the pitch faces a likely defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a football field after the Gillingham clue, but it is musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tone-deaf describes someone unable to distinguish differences in musical pitch.

clue.text: Savage Northern bird

parts.note: savage, as in harsh and cruel, is bitter

explanation.surface: A fierce bird from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading bird of the heron family, known for its booming call.

clue.text: I may appear in Twilight of the Gods

indicators.note: may appear in says the answer shows up inside the title that follows

explanation.surface: Someone imagining appearing in Wagner's opera Twilight of the Gods.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'thE GOds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is Latin for 'I', and means one's sense of self.

clue.text: Break down in north of Devon is with school

indicators.note: in a down clue north of means the top, so the first letter

parts.note: a sect is a school of thought or religious group

explanation.surface: A school pupil in north Devon breaks down in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is an English county; its 'north' in a down clue is its first letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect is to cut apart for study, and so to analyse in detail, to break down.

clue.text: Aunt fed onions to gathering as basic necessity

indicators.note: gathering suggests the words are collected up and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An aunt fed onions to a party of guests as a staple of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' looks like the guests being fed, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a foundation stone is the base on which everything else depends, a basic necessity.

clue.text: Article on uncompleted highest city in Egypt

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: uncompleted means the last letter is left off

parts.note: best is the highest in quality

explanation.surface: A piece about an unfinished summit of an Egyptian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncompleted' cuts BEST to BES.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was the great ancient Egyptian capital on the Nile, near modern Luxor.

clue.text: A small but valuable piece of bomb turning up in Brazil, perhaps

indicators.note: in says the turned piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a Brazil is an example of a nut

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: egg is old RAF slang for a bomb

explanation.surface: A fragment of a bomb found in Brazil turns out to be precious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil' reads as the country but is a Brazil nut. 'turning up' reverses EGG to GGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small lump of gold, or by extension any small but valuable item.

clue.text: Energy required round start of daily grind

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: power means energy

indicators.note: start of means take the first letter

explanation.surface: Effort is needed to start the daily routine, the daily grind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily grind' looks like a phrase, but 'grind' alone is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To powder something is to crush it into fine particles, which is to grind it.

clue.text: Cultural period shows individual in setting

indicators.note: in says the single one goes inside the setting

parts.note: a stage is a setting or scene for events
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A cultural era reveals the individual against their surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric period defined by the culture of stone tool use.

clue.text: Frost Report's second in command promoted?

indicators.note: promoted means moved up ahead, so the command abbreviation comes before the letter

parts.note: IC is the abbreviation for 'in charge' or 'in command'

indicators.note: second means the second letter

explanation.surface: On the TV satire The Frost Report, a deputy gets promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Frost Report was a 1960s BBC comedy show hosted by David Frost. 'promoted' puts IC in front of E.
explanation.definitionFit: Frost is a coating of ice crystals, so ice serves as an example of frost.

clue.text: I fall behind in Kent getting fodder

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the region's letters

parts.note: Kent is in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
to lag is to fall behind

explanation.surface: A Kent farmer falls behind in getting animal feed in.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the South East of England, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is grass or other green crops stored in a silo as winter feed for livestock.

clue.text: Got together, misled about furthest points of voyage

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other piece

parts.note: conned means tricked or misled

indicators.note: furthest points of means the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A group assembled after being deceived about the far reaches of a sea journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container: the word for misled wraps round the ends of the journey word.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to meet or assemble, so convened means gathered together.
